subject: Social Media
title: The Chronological Feed
description: Learn The Chronological Feed in one minute.

hook.text: In 2004, your Facebook feed was simple. Newest post first. You saw everything your friends shared.

buildup.text: Every platform started this way. Twitter, Instagram, Tumblr—all chronological. Fair and square.

discovery.text: By 2010, users followed hundreds of accounts. Great posts vanished in the flood of new content.

twist.text: Users missed 70% of posts. The chronological feed wasn't fair—it rewarded timing, not quality.

climax.text: Facebook quietly tested ranked feeds. Engagement jumped. Users stayed longer and saw more ads.

punchline.text: The timeline died so the algorithm could live.

quiz.question: What main problem did chronological feeds have by 2010?
